source: committed round batches of the 5 donor arms, compose-pmo-donor-qual, transplant_share=0.5
answers_the_question: The lane does NOT fail to generate useful grafts, and the controller does NOT systematically discard them. Donor attempts carry a median 14 surviving new atoms against 4 for every other proposal -- exactly the >=13-atom structural scale the global-delta census measured as required by 58.3% of productive transitions and reached by the controller on only 0.4% of proposals. Donor transplants also NEVER fail execution (0% vs 18.3%), because they are valid by construction. They are charged roughly in proportion to their share of the stream (3.8% of charged against 5.8% of attempts), so selection is not the bottleneck either.
the_two_real_defects: 51.3% of donor attempts are DUPLICATES against 5.7% for everything else -- a 9x rate. The lane keeps redrawing (donor, cut) pairs it has already produced, so half its budget buys nothing.

Donor reaches only ~5.8% of attempts at transplant_share=0.5, because recombination is one proposal kind among many. A mechanism with a 6% footprint cannot move AUC, so the matched A/B is underpowered BY CONSTRUCTION -- the same 'effect cannot exceed footprint' problem that made the completion-law A/B a throttle test.
consequence: Do NOT integrate donor into the combined controller on this evidence, and do NOT tune transplant share/timeout/ceiling/cuts. But the null is NOT evidence that large structural transplantation is useless: it is evidence that this lane's draw is half-wasted and too small a share of the stream to be measurable. The reusable finding is that the transplant generator produces the right structural scale, which is what the next mechanism needs to preserve.
caveat: Arms are 48-336 charged calls in. These are PROPOSAL-STREAM statistics, which are far better powered than the AUC comparison (20,328 attempts), but say nothing directly about final score.
